newsitem.title: USA: Kyzen sees improved revenue growth in H2.
newsitem.headline: Kyzen sees improved revenue growth in H2.

text.p: Kyzen Corp said Tuesday that the company's growth rate of revenues was lower than usual for the first two quarters of fiscal 1997 but should improve in the second half of the year.
The company said it is trending towards profitability, as overall costs should remain constant and revenues grow in the latter half of 1997.
Kyzen reported a second quarter loss of $0.02 a share on revenues of $1.3 million compared with a loss of $0.03 a share on revenues of $2.6 million for the previous second quarter.

Kyzen said it expects revenue growth to benefit as new customer installations come on line following the reconfiguring of plants and installation of new cleaning equipment that typically occurs during the summer.

The company said that while year-to-year sales for the second quarter were up slightly, sales for this year's second quarter were below annualized growth rate expectations due primarily to the timing of certain large recurring international and aerospace orders. These orders, which were expected to book and ship late in the second quarter, were not booked and shipped until early in the third quarter.

Kyzen said that when compared with last year's second quarter, the 1997 second quarter loss decreased sharply on a modest revenue increase principally because of product mix improvements, led by the company's new PCS control devices in the equipment area, and level to declining costs in all departments.

Research and development spending for the second quarter of this year decreased 38 percent compared with last year primarily due to a reduction in development expenses for the company's machine product line.

Quarterly R&D expense should remain steady at approximately the same level as this year's second quarter due to a decrease in development associated with equipment and a greater focus on its chemical product lines, it said.
